session.name: MPI-600 Leg A pass 1 - LoRA question CLOSED, base weight converted, two settings traps found that invalidate 27 of 36 rows

goal.original: Bench FLUX.2 Klein 9B - base vs turbo LoRA vs distilled vs KV - and pick the weight MPI-598 ships.
goal.summary: Leg A's one open question is answered: the rank-128 turbo LoRA DOES apply to an INT8 ConvRot base (121 patches attached vs 0 without), so fp8 is not forced and there is no asymmetry. Getting there required CONVERTING the base weight, which native ComfyUI cannot load at all. A full 36-run Leg A matrix then ran and is recorded - but only the 9 turbo-100 rows are valid. Two settings traps, both found by opening the PNGs rather than reading the table, invalidate the rest. Legs B and C have not started.

completed: THE OPEN QUESTION IS CLOSED - klein_9B_Turbo_r128 applies to an INT8 ConvRot base. Proof: the bench log prints 'Model Flux2 ... 121 patches attached' with the LoRA and '0 patches attached' without, no 'lora key not loaded' warnings, and the pixels differ. fp8 stays off the table.

THE BASE WEIGHT HAD TO BE CONVERTED - flux-2-klein-base-9b-int8-ConvRot.safetensors (bertbobson) dies in node 27 with 'Unknown quantization format for layer double_blocks.0.img_attn.qkv'. Its per-layer comfy_quant is {"convrot": true} with no 'format' key; comfy/ops.py:1163 reads layer_conf.get('format') and raises on None. Converted with the uploader's own documented tool (vendored as research/convert_to_comfy.py) - 114/114 markers rewritten, all 429 tensors otherwise unchanged, verified. USE flux-2-klein-base-9b-int8-convrot-comfy.safetensors; the original is kept and is still unloadable.

THE FILENAMES LIE - distilled and KV are {"format": "int8_tensorwise"} with SCALAR weight_scale, i.e. plain tensorwise INT8, NOT ConvRot. Only the base arm is genuinely ConvRot (per-row [4096,1] scales, like the shipped 4B). Legs B and C carry a quantisation confound.
research/results.md created and filled with a complete 36-row Leg A matrix (4 arms x 3 scenarios x 3 seeds), plus a validity section stating exactly which rows survive
research/sweep.py written - the arm x scenario x seed driver; frees the bench before every run so every VRAM number is real; scores S2 through seam.py automatically

Wall clock is linear in steps at 1024^2: 8 steps 32 s, 10 steps 48 s, 20 steps 82 s, plus ~8 s constant load. cfg > 1 adds the uncond pass (turbo-035 costs 40 s at the same 8 steps turbo-100 runs in 32 s).

VRAM is flat across every arm and both branches: ~14.3-15.0 GB attributable, 15.2-15.8 GB peak against 16380 MiB. The turbo LoRA costs nothing measurable. The base arm sits slightly HIGHER than Leg 0's distilled reading.
The bench is exactly reproducible - the same seed and graph reproduced a seam triple to three decimals across two separate invocations, so arm-to-arm differences are real signal.

The colouring question re-confirmed on Leg A: outside-mask mean signed -0.742/255, ring 64-128 px max delta 5, ring 128+ px max delta 0 (byte-identical). No colour cast even when the edit itself fails.
pending: LEG A PASS 2 - re-run base, turbo-070 and turbo-035 with --set 52.boolean=false. 27 of the 36 rows are invalid without it. The 9 turbo-100 rows stand and need no re-run.

S2R - run sweep.py --s2-regime (all four arms). S2 has never actually tested any arm, because branch 5 hardcodes 2 steps / cfg 1. This decides whether base/turbo can do a localised edit at all, and whether that hardcode is a shipping blocker for MPI-598.
Leg B - base+turbo@1.0 vs distilled; and whether intermediate strengths reach quality distilled cannot (decides one checkpoint or two). Record the ConvRot-vs-tensorwise confound on every row.
Leg C - 9b-kv vs the leg-B winner, edit scenarios only, recording ref count and output resolution per row
research/verdict.md answering the four deliverable questions, then post it onto MPI-598

OPEN EVERY PNG AS IT LANDS - both traps produced perfectly plausible wall-clock, VRAM and seam numbers while the images were invalid, and neither raised an error. key_decisions: Fabio 2026-08-22: stop mid-sweep, gather the findings and hand off rather than burn a large context finishing runs that were already known to be invalid.

Fabio 2026-08-22: LOOK AT THE OUTPUTS AS THEY COME IN. This session recorded 36 rows of plausible numbers before opening a single PNG; two structural faults were sitting in the images the whole time. This is now a standing instruction for the remaining legs.

The base arm's steps/cfg (20 / 5.0) and the turbo rows come from README's per-arm table; they are the template's own numbers and a starting point, not a measurement. Pass 2 should confirm base actually needs 20 steps once its negative is real.
Scenarios stay LOCKED as in research/scenarios.md - 3 scenarios x 3 seeds. Nothing about these findings changes the scenario definitions.
constraints: NODE 52 IS NOT JUST A NUMBERS SWITCH. Input_is_Turbo (52) drives MpiIfElse 57/212/222, which swap the negative between ConditioningZeroOut (true) and the real CLIPTextEncode (false). Left true, any arm at cfg > 1 amplifies against a zero negative and blows out - neon grass, cyan sky, posterised edges. It reads as 'the model is bad' and is nothing of the sort. Set 52.boolean=false whenever cfg > 1; at cfg 1.0 it is irrelevant.

THE wf_type 5 BRANCH IGNORES NODES 203/204. It samples through 252, whose sigmas come from 267 (steps: 2 HARDCODED) and whose guider 254 has cfg: 1 HARDCODED. Only branches 1 (28/31/32) and 4 (185/173/170) honour the steps/cfg knobs. The tell is wall clock - base S1 at 20 steps took 82 s, base S2 'at 20 steps' took 16 s. Drive 267.steps and 254.cfg directly; no graph edit is needed because run.py --set reaches any input.

Branch 5 paints the masked region PURE GREEN (ImageCompositeMasked, colour 65280) and regenerates it. At 2 steps an undistilled base cannot, so the green SURVIVES INTO THE SAVED PNG. If you see green, the edit failed - it is not a temp file and not a test artifact. seam.py on such a run scores the edge of a green blob, not a seam.
USE flux-2-klein-base-9b-int8-convrot-comfy.safetensors for every base arm. The originally downloaded base weight cannot be loaded by native ComfyUI at all.
A VRAM READING IS A LIE UNLESS YOU FREE THE BENCH FIRST - POST /free {"unload_models":true,"free_memory":true} to :8188, sample the floor, then run. sweep.py already does this before every run.

Reading /internal/logs/raw through Windows cp1252 dies with UnicodeEncodeError on the tqdm bar - encode with .encode('ascii','replace') before printing. 'N patches attached' in that log is the instrument for whether a LoRA applied.
Bench is :8188, the app engine is :48188 - never drive :3000, which is Fabio's live app.
MpiClearVram (node 570) does NOT force a cold run - it offloads VRAM->RAM. Leave it in the chain; do not 'fix' it.
